subject: Veridian AI — post-demo checklist & migration playbook
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Michael Yang <michael.yang@veridian.ai>, Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Veridian AI — post-demo checklist & migration playbook

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the candid signals on scale and compliance. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can shape an accurate proposal and migration plan.

What we covered
- Demo highlights: streaming latency under 120ms (p50) on our Dedicated profile; built-in prefix caching for chat workloads; deterministic fallbacks for capacity events.
- Migration options: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated reserved pools (predictable throughput, private tenancy), Private VPC (data residency + on-prem connector).

Questions to help us recommend an exact path
1) Current production traffic pattern: you mentioned bursts up to ~1M tokens/day. Is that steady or seasonal?
2) Source of current traffic: you said most traffic flows through OpenAI’s API today — any components still on a self-hosted GPU cluster (e.g., for offline batch rerank)?
3) Data residency / encryption: do you require customer-managed keys and strictly US-only egress?

Suggested immediate next steps
- We can draft a 90-day Dedicated ramp (2x8-GPU nodes) with a billing ramp and a short-term promo credit to cover the POC period.
- If procurement wants an initial PO first, I can share a PO template and the basic SOW for migration.
- Technical kickoff: propose Dec 6 for a 1-hour runbook walkthrough (eng + infra).

Attachments: I’ve attached a short migration playbook and a PO template for procurement review.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the answers above and procurement contact to land the PO cadence.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Yang <michael.yang@veridian.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@veridian.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Veridian AI — post-demo checklist & migration playbook

Kimberly — thanks for the recap and clear next steps. A few quick answers and clarifications: 

- Traffic: the ~1M tokens/day is our current steady state for the customer-facing chat surface; we also have nightly batch reranks (approx 100M tokens/day) on a self-hosted GPU cluster that we plan to migrate over the next 3–6 months.
- Source: majority through OpenAI API; batch jobs and an internal prototype still on an in-house cluster (two A100 boxes).
- Residency/KMS: must be US-only egress; procurement will need SOC2 Type II evidence and we use AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK for production keys.

Procurement: looping in procurement@veridian.ai. They’ll want the PO template and SOW before the legal exchange. Also please add any SOC2 report links or compliance pack in the same thread.

Tentative: Dec 6 works for an engineering kickoff. For the runbook, could you call out migration options for the batch rerank jobs (lift-and-shift vs hybrid fallback)? We’re sensitive to model parity during cutover.

Appreciate it — will review attachments and get procurement’s contact details.

—Michael
Michael Yang
VP Engineering, Veridian.ai
michael.yang@veridian.ai

This reduces parity risk while giving predictable latency for live traffic.
